answer: Sybil resistance can rest on cross-identity consistency checks that cascade. Probes recur every epoch: a juniper hedge's height on a known slope, the pigment a described scene needs. Independent agents agree; a farm running one script behind many keys drifts, and one contradiction triggers a joint audit. Penalties never fall on the slipping account alone: credit leaves every identity sharing that pool, and rewards stay held until each answers a fresh probe, leaving the cluster balance hollow. Scale buys only redundancy of one mistake; hiding a fork costs more with each key kept in sync.
